svg.title: SDLT and LTT rates - residential and non-residential kept apart - SQE1 12.2
svg.desc: Poster showing separate residential and non-residential rate ladders for SDLT in England and LTT in Wales, plus filing deadlines and CGT.
svg.text: SQE1 §12.2 · RESIDENTIAL and NON-RESIDENTIAL are separate ladders — never mix them
ENGLAND · HMRC · SDLT1 in 14 days · SDLT5 for HMLR
WALES · WRA · return in 30 days · receipt for HMLR
Consideration of £40,000 or more → you must file the return, even where the tax is £0.
Tax only starts ABOVE the nil band:
R E S I D E N T I A L — dwellings and their grounds
England only — no equivalent in Wales
NO first-time buyer relief in Wales
N O N - R E S I D E N T I A L / M I X E D U S E — shops, offices, farmland, flat-over-shop, 6+ dwellings
Up to £150,000 — note £150,000, NOT the residential £125,000
GRANT OF A LEASE — you may pay TWICE: on the PREMIUM (ladders above) and on the RENT (net present value)
SDLT residential rent: 1% on the NPV above £125,000
SDLT non-residential rent: 0% to £150,000 · 1% to £5m · 2% above £5m
LTT residential rent: NO charge on rent
LTT non-residential rent: 0% to £225,000 · 1% to £2m · 2% above £2m
Assignment of an existing lease → price only, no NPV charge
CGT ON A LATER DISPOSAL — charged on the GAIN, and the rate depends on where the gain falls in your income
only or main home throughout = exempt, s.222 TCGA 1992
The test is what the PROPERTY is, not who the buyer is. · Any commercial element, or 6+ dwellings in one transaction → NON-RESIDENTIAL ladder. · A buy-to-let house is still RESIDENTIAL.
